Banking
(Amendment)
Act 2016
The enactment of this Act

capped the lending rate at a
maximum of 4% above the
CBR whilst capping the
minimum deposit rate to
70% of the CBR.

The effect of the imple-
mentation of the Act was
witnessed across the
banking industry in the
last quarter of 2016 where
there was a 2% reduction
in gross loan growth. The
expectation is that banks
will enhance credit
standards and require-
ments for customers even
as they embrace conserva-
tive lending in favor of
investing in treasury bills.
In addition, growth in
profitability in 2017 is also
expected to be muted due
to shrinking margins.

DTB will continue to invest
in the future - principally
in its people, technology
and innovation - with a
particular bias on new,
digital- anchored channels,
products and services- so
that it is well pivoted as a
strong, Tier I bank in all its
principal markets, playing
an effective financial
intermediary role across
the communities it
operates in.
